response.sql:
WITH joined AS (
  SELECT f.orderslink, o.ordertune, f.rebtotal, (f.rebrate - f.feerate) / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0) AS relgap
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink
),
grp AS (
  SELECT orderslink, ordertune, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebate, AVG(relgap) AS avg_relgap
  FROM joined
  GROUP BY orderslink, ordertune
),
base AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rebate) AS baseline FROM grp
)
SELECT g.orderslink, g.ordertune AS order_type, g.avg_rebate, g.avg_relgap, g.avg_rebate - b.baseline AS excess_over_baseline
FROM grp g
CROSS JOIN base b
WHERE g.avg_rebate > b.baseline
ORDER BY excess_over_baseline DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: orders.recordvault is unique, as the documentation states, so the inner join adds no duplicate fee rows; fees with no matching order are dropped by the inner join.
A zero or NULL feerate makes the relative gap NULL (via NULLIF), and AVG skips it, so those fees still count toward the average rebate but not the average gap.
The baseline is the AVG of group-level average rebates; groups whose average rebate is NULL are left out of it, and no group whose average rebate is NULL can pass the > baseline filter.
Orders with a NULL ordertune are kept as their own group (GROUP BY treats NULLs as one group) rather than dropped; the request does not say which to do.
Grouping by orderslink and ordertune is effectively per order, since each orderslink maps to one order and so to one ordertune.

alternatives.interpretation: Drop orders with no order type (NULL ordertune) before grouping, so only groups with a known order type are ranked and counted in the baseline.
alternatives.sql:
WITH joined AS (
  SELECT f.orderslink, o.ordertune, f.rebtotal, (f.rebrate - f.feerate) / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0) AS relgap
  FROM fees f
  JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink
  WHERE o.ordertune IS NOT NULL
),
grp AS (
  SELECT orderslink, ordertune, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebate, AVG(relgap) AS avg_relgap
  FROM joined
  GROUP BY orderslink, ordertune
),
base AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rebate) AS baseline FROM grp
)
SELECT g.orderslink, g.ordertune AS order_type, g.avg_rebate, g.avg_relgap, g.avg_rebate - b.baseline AS excess_over_baseline
FROM grp g
CROSS JOIN base b
WHERE g.avg_rebate > b.baseline
ORDER BY excess_over_baseline DESC
LIMIT 10;
